create.name: Soji Zen Center
create.bio:
Soji Zen Center is a Zen sangha in Drexel Hill, Pennsylvania, started by Roshi Jules Shuzen Harris in 2005. Harris trained with John Daido Loori and Dennis Genpo Merzel before receiving dharma transmission, and in 2019 inka, from Roshi Pat Enkyo O'Hara of the Village Zendo in New York; no African-American man had received Soto transmission before him, and he started Soji so that the dharma would be open to people whatever their race or means. The centre belongs to the White Plum lineage, which draws on both Soto and Rinzai Zen. Since Harris's death in 2023 the sangha has been led by his dharma heir, Sensei John Ango Gruber, together with Sensei Annalisa Rakugo Castaldo and Sensei Anthony Nentetsu Yuschak.

Practice rests on zazen, liturgy and the study of Buddhist texts. Sunday mornings bring a service, three periods of sitting and a dharma talk, and on Tuesday evenings there is sitting with the chance of a private interview; both run in person and on Zoom, with online morning sittings twice a week as well. A monthly one-day retreat, occasional workshops and a disability affinity group fill out the year, and a large archive of Harris's recorded talks can be heard free on the website.

courses.title: One-Day Retreat (Zazenkai)
courses.description: The centre's monthly day of silent practice, running from mid-morning to late afternoon with periods of zazen, open both at the Drexel Hill zendo and online. The calendar lists each date and how to register.

free_resources.title: Virtual Zendo
free_resources.description: Zoom links and guidance for sitting with the sangha online: Sunday service with zazen and a talk, and shorter morning and evening sittings during the week, with the sutra book to chant along.

free_resources.title: Dharma Talks by Shuzen Roshi
free_resources.description: An archive of recorded talks by the founder, Roshi Jules Shuzen Harris, on koans from the Mumonkan, Dogen's Genjokoan, the four seals and practice in daily life, playable or downloadable as audio.
